content.text: Enter Dogberry, Verges, and Sexton, in gowns; and the Watch, with Conrade and Borachio.

lines.text: Is our whole dissembly appeared?
lines.plainText: Is our whole dissembly appeared

lines.text: O! a stool and a cushion for the sexton.
lines.plainText: O a stool and a cushion for the sexton

lines.text: Which be the malefactors?
lines.plainText: Which be the malefactors

lines.text: Marry, that am I and my partner.
lines.plainText: Marry that am I and my partner

lines.text: Nay, that's certain: we have the exhibition to examine.
lines.plainText: Nay that's certain we have the exhibition to examine

lines.text: But which are the offenders that are to be examined? let them come before Master Constable.
lines.plainText: But which are the offenders that are to be examined let them come before Master Constable

lines.text: Yea, marry, let them come before me. What is your name, friend?
lines.plainText: Yea marry let them come before me What is your name friend

lines.text: Borachio.
lines.plainText: Borachio

lines.text: Pray write down Borachio. Yours, sirrah?
lines.plainText: Pray write down Borachio Yours sirrah

lines.text: I am a gentleman, sir, and my name is Conrade.
lines.plainText: I am a gentleman sir and my name is Conrade

lines.text: Write down Master gentleman Conrade. Masters, do you serve God?
lines.plainText: Write down Master gentleman Conrade Masters do you serve God

lines.text: Yea, sir, we hope.
lines.plainText: Yea sir we hope

lines.text: Write down that they hope they serve God: and write God first; for God defend but God should go before such villains! Masters, it is proved already that you are little better than false knaves, and it will go near to be thought so shortly. How answer you for yourselves?
lines.plainText: Write down that they hope they serve God and write God first for God defend but God should go before such villains Masters it is proved already that you are little better than false knaves and it will go near to be thought so shortly How answer you for yourselves

lines.text: Marry, sir, we say we are none.
lines.plainText: Marry sir we say we are none

lines.text: A marvellous witty fellow, I assure you; but I will go about with him. Come you hither, sirrah; a word in your ear: sir, I say to you, it is thought you are false knaves.
lines.plainText: A marvellous witty fellow I assure you but I will go about with him Come you hither sirrah a word in your ear sir I say to you it is thought you are false knaves

lines.text: Sir, I say to you we are none.
lines.plainText: Sir I say to you we are none

lines.text: Well, stand aside. Fore God, they are both in a tale. Have you writ down, that they are none?
lines.plainText: Well stand aside Fore God they are both in a tale Have you writ down that they are none

lines.text: Master Constable, you go not the way to examine: you must call forth the watch that are their accusers.
lines.plainText: Master Constable you go not the way to examine you must call forth the watch that are their accusers

lines.text: Yea, marry, that's the eftest way. Let the watch come forth. Masters, I charge you, in the Prince's name, accuse these men.
lines.plainText: Yea marry that's the eftest way Let the watch come forth Masters I charge you in the Prince's name accuse these men

lines.text: This man said, sir, that Don John, the Prince's brother, was a villain.
lines.plainText: This man said sir that Don John the Prince's brother was a villain

lines.text: Write down Prince John a villain. Why, this is flat perjury, to call a Prince's brother villain.
lines.plainText: Write down Prince John a villain Why this is flat perjury to call a Prince's brother villain

lines.text: Master Constable,—
lines.plainText: Master Constable

lines.text: Pray thee, fellow, peace: I do not like thy look, I promise thee.
lines.plainText: Pray thee fellow peace I do not like thy look I promise thee

lines.text: What heard you him say else?
lines.plainText: What heard you him say else

lines.text: Marry, that he had received a thousand ducats of Don John for accusing the Lady Hero wrongfully.
lines.plainText: Marry that he had received a thousand ducats of Don John for accusing the Lady Hero wrongfully

lines.text: Flat burglary as ever was committed.
lines.plainText: Flat burglary as ever was committed

lines.text: Yea, by the mass, that it is.
lines.plainText: Yea by the mass that it is

lines.text: What else, fellow?
lines.plainText: What else fellow

lines.text: And that Count Claudio did mean, upon his words, to disgrace Hero before the whole assembly, and not marry her.
lines.plainText: And that Count Claudio did mean upon his words to disgrace Hero before the whole assembly and not marry her

lines.text: O villain! thou wilt be condemned into everlasting redemption for this.
lines.plainText: O villain thou wilt be condemned into everlasting redemption for this

lines.text: What else?
lines.plainText: What else

lines.text: This is all.
lines.plainText: This is all

lines.text: And this is more, masters, than you can deny. Prince John is this morning secretly stolen away: Hero was in this manner accused, in this manner refused, and, upon the grief of this, suddenly died. Master Constable, let these men be bound, and brought to Leonato's: I will go before and show him their examination.
lines.plainText: And this is more masters than you can deny Prince John is this morning secretly stolen away Hero was in this manner accused in this manner refused and upon the grief of this suddenly died Master Constable let these men be bound and brought to Leonato's I will go before and show him their examination

lines.text: Come, let them be opinioned.
lines.plainText: Come let them be opinioned

lines.text: Let them be in the hands—
lines.plainText: Let them be in the hands

lines.text: Off, coxcomb!
lines.plainText: Off coxcomb

lines.text: God's my life! where's the sexton? let him write down the Prince's officer coxcomb. Come, bind them. Thou naughty varlet!
lines.plainText: God's my life where's the sexton let him write down the Prince's officer coxcomb Come bind them Thou naughty varlet

lines.text: Away! you are an ass; you are an ass.
lines.plainText: Away you are an ass you are an ass

lines.text: Dost thou not suspect my place? Dost thou not suspect my years? O that he were here to write me down an ass! but, masters, remember that I am an ass; though it be not written down, yet forget not that I am an ass. No, thou villain, thou art full of piety, as shall be proved upon thee by good witness. I am a wise fellow; and, which is more, an officer; and, which is more, a householder; and, which is more, as pretty a piece of flesh as any in Messina; and one that knows the law, go to; and a rich fellow enough, go to; and a fellow that hath had losses; and one that hath two gowns, and everything handsome about him. Bring him away. O that I had been writ down an ass!
